title: Performance Efficiency — Time Behaviour & Resource Utilization
problem: How to guarantee deterministic sub-second response times and bounded CPU/memory utilization under high-frequency ingestion?
summary: Measures response/processing times, throughput rates, and resource consumption under stated load conditions. Sub-second latency (<1s p99) requires bounded serialization overhead, non-blocking I/O, and partitioned log or in-memory streaming.

title: Reliability — Availability, Fault Tolerance & Recoverability
problem: How to ensure continuous operation and zero data loss during hardware, network, or downstream service failures?
summary: Degree to which a system remains operational and recovers state after hardware/network faults. High availability (99.99%+) requires quorum replication (RAFT/ISR), automated failover, bulkhead isolation, and durable write-ahead logs.

title: Security — Confidentiality, Integrity, Non-Repudiation & Accountability
problem: How to enforce authentication, authorization, and tamper-evident auditability across internal and regulatory boundaries?
summary: Ensures data is accessible only to authorized actors, prevents tampering, and guarantees immutable audit trails. Zero-trust architectures mandate mutual TLS (mTLS), RBAC/ABAC policy enforcement, and append-only cryptographic audit logs.

title: Maintainability — Modularity, Modifiability & Operability Burden
problem: How to align architectural complexity with the engineering and operations team's cognitive load capacity?
summary: Assesses how effectively a system can be modified, deployed, and operated by the engineering team. Distributed architectures (microservices, multi-broker clusters) introduce high operational complexity that can overwhelm small teams (<6 engineers).

title: Lightweight Event Streaming (NATS JetStream / Redpanda Single-Binary)
source: CNCF Messaging Benchmark & Cloud Native Patterns (2025)
problem: How to ingest high-frequency factory/IoT telemetry with <1s latency on-premise when operated by a lean (<=5 person) engineering team?
summary: Single-binary event streaming brokers (NATS JetStream in Go, Redpanda in C++) eliminate JVM/ZooKeeper operational overhead while providing persistent streams, consumer groups, at-least-once delivery, and <5ms p99 latency. Ideal for edge/on-prem and small ops teams.

title: Enterprise Distributed Log (Apache Kafka + Strimzi Kubernetes Operator)
problem: How to provide high-throughput partitioned event streaming with long-term retention when a mature Kubernetes platform team is available?
options: Apache Kafka on Kubernetes with Strimzi Operator (KRaft mode)
summary: Apache Kafka provides industry-standard high-throughput partitioned log storage (>1M msg/s), rich Kafka Connect ecosystem, and long-term tiered retention. While historically heavy to operate, Kubernetes Operators (Strimzi) automate rolling upgrades and KRaft eliminates ZooKeeper.

title: Modular Monolith with Explicit Domain Boundaries
source: Software Architecture: The Hard Parts (Ford, Richards, Sadalage)
problem: How to structure a business application for fast delivery and clean domain separation when built by a small team (<=6 devs) without dedicated SREs?
options: Modular Monolith with Explicit Domain Boundaries & Single PostgreSQL
summary: Deploys a single application unit with strictly enforced internal module boundaries (compile-time package isolation and separate database schemas per module). Avoids distributed network latency, distributed transactions, and DevOps sprawl while preserving future extraction paths.

title: Fine-Grained Microservices with API Gateway & Service Mesh
problem: How to enable 10+ autonomous engineering squads (100+ developers) to deploy independently without release-train bottlenecks?
options: Domain-Aligned Microservices with API Gateway, Contract Testing & Platform PaaS
summary: Independent deployment, polyglot persistence, and isolated fault domains per bounded context. Requires mature CI/CD, distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), automated canary deployments, and dedicated platform engineering support.

title: CQRS with Event Sourcing vs. Read-Replica Projection
source: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture & DDD Catalog
problem: When to use an append-only cryptographic event log (Event Sourcing) versus lightweight Read Replicas + Cache-Aside?
options: Event Sourcing with Append-Only Cryptographically Chained Log in PostgreSQL
Primary PostgreSQL + Read Replicas + Cache-Aside Redis
summary: Full Event Sourcing stores state as an immutable sequence of domain events, providing complete auditability and temporal queries. Lightweight Read-Replica + Redis Cache-Aside serves 99% read workloads in <10ms without event-store complexity.

title: Saga Pattern: Orchestrated (Workflow Engine) vs. Choreographed (Events)
problem: How to coordinate multi-step (7-8 steps) distributed workflows with long-running timeouts and compensating rollbacks?
options: Orchestrated Saga via Durable Workflow Engine (Temporal / State Machine)
summary: Orchestrated sagas (e.g., Temporal, Camunda, State Machine) centralize multi-step workflow coordination, compensation logic, and timeout handling, preventing cyclic event spaghetti when workflows exceed 3-4 steps. Choreography suits simple 2-3 step decoupled notifications.

title: Time-Series & Analytical Storage: TimescaleDB vs. ClickHouse vs. InfluxDB
source: Industrial IoT & Semiconductor Telemetry Reference Architecture
problem: How to store 50k-80k sensor readings/sec on-premise while supporting native SQL joins with relational PostgreSQL metadata?
summary: TimescaleDB (PostgreSQL extension) combines relational metadata joins, ACID familiarity, and automatic hypertable compression for moderate telemetry (<200k metrics/sec). ClickHouse excels at massive columnar OLAP aggregations (>1M rows/sec) with extreme compression ratios.

title: Edge-First Hierarchical Buffering (Store-and-Forward Gateway)
source: Industrial Edge Computing & Smart Manufacturing Patterns
problem: How to guarantee zero telemetry loss and <200ms local safety control when WAN connectivity to headquarters drops for hours?
options: Edge-First Store-and-Forward Gateway (Local NATS Leaf / SQLite Buffer)
summary: Places local edge gateways (SQLite/RocksDB/local NATS leaf nodes) at factory lines to filter, aggregate, and buffer high-frequency sensor data during WAN link outages, syncing asynchronously to central cloud/on-prem clusters.

title: Transactional Outbox + CDC (Debezium) vs. Polling Publisher
source: Bass, Clements, Kazman — Software Architecture in Practice (4th Ed.)
problem: How to eliminate dual-write inconsistencies between PostgreSQL updates and message broker publication without adding heavy infrastructure?
options: Transactional Outbox Table with Lightweight Polling Publisher
Transactional Outbox with Full Debezium + Kafka Connect Cluster
summary: Guarantees dual-write consistency between relational DB updates and message broker publication. Polling Outbox requires zero extra infrastructure beyond the relational DB; Log-based CDC (Debezium) offers lower latency but adds Kafka Connect operational overhead.

title: Resilience Tactics: Circuit Breaker, Adaptive Concurrency Limit & Bulkhead
source: Release It! (Michael Nygard) & SEI Availability Tactics
problem: How to prevent a slow or hanging external/legacy dependency from exhausting worker threads and crashing the entire service?
options: Bulkhead Thread/Connection Pool Isolation + Circuit Breaker with Fallback Queue
summary: Prevents cascading failures across synchronous dependencies by isolating thread/connection pools per downstream service (Bulkhead) and shedding load fast when error rates or p99 latencies breach thresholds.

title: Zero-Trust Security Tactics: mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE vs. API Gateway OAuth2/JWT
problem: How to secure 3-4 internal services in a single Kubernetes cluster managed by a small (2-3 person) team?
options: API Gateway with OIDC/OAuth2 JWT Validation + K8s NetworkPolicies
Full Multi-Cluster Istio Service Mesh + SPIFFE/SPIRE
summary: Cryptographic workload identity (SPIFFE/SPIRE + mTLS) enforces mutual authentication and encryption in transit for east-west traffic. For smaller deployments, external OAuth2/OIDC validation at the ingress gateway with network policies balances security and complexity.

title: Legacy Modernization: Strangler Fig Pattern with Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
problem: How to replace a 15-20 year old mission-critical monolithic ERP/MES system with zero production downtime?
options: Strangler Fig Pattern with Routing Facade & Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
summary: Incrementally replaces legacy ERP/MES systems by routing specific vertical slices through a proxy facade and translating legacy data models via an Anti-Corruption Layer, avoiding high-risk 'big bang' rewrites.

title: ORG-PRINCIPLE-01: Operational Proportionality (Team Cognitive Load Cap)
problem: How to prevent Day-2 operational outages caused by over-complex distributed infrastructure in small teams?
options: Single-Binary / Consolidated Engines (NATS, Modular Monolith, TimescaleDB, Polling Outbox)
summary: Architectural complexity must scale proportionally to Operations team headcount. For teams with <= 5 SRE/Ops engineers, managed services or single-binary/consolidated technologies (e.g., NATS JetStream, Modular Monolith, PostgreSQL+TimescaleDB) are strongly preferred over multi-cluster distributed ecosystems.

title: ORG-PRINCIPLE-02: Strict Data Sovereignty & Sub-Second Factory Floor Control
problem: Where must wafer fabrication telemetry and real-time equipment control loops execute?
summary: Wafer fabrication and cleanroom equipment telemetry must remain on-premise or within air-gapped factory zones with deterministic <1s alerting latency; public cloud round-trips are prohibited for critical real-time control loops.
